language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, my name is Chip!
Hello. My name is Kyan. You already know many things about circles and triangles.
Let's review things about circles and triangles.
Notice how the circle has a center. The center of a circle is the point in the middle of the circle.
A circle's circumference is the distance around the edge of the circle.
A circle's radius is the distance from the center to the edge. Radii is plural of a radius.
A different part of the circle is a Sector.
This is a part of a circled enclosed by two radii of a circle and their intercepted arc.
The Diameter of a circle starts at one side of the circle, goes through the center and ends at the other side.
Half a circle is called a Semicircle.
Let's take a closer look at triangles. A triangle is a three-sided polygon whose interior angles' sum is always 180°
Let's look at four different kinds of triangles: isosceles, equilateral, scalene, and right-angle triangles.
An Equilateral Triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles.
A Scalene Triangle has no equal sides and no equal angles.
A Right-angle Triangle has a right angle (90°).
An Isosceles Triangle has two equal sides and two equal angles.
Let's practice with circles and triangles!
